Sound familiar? Well, what if building real wealth doesn't actually require destroying your mental health and social life? Most people think financial independence is brutal suffering for decades. But the people who actually build serious wealth without
script.ending_words: which means letting your money do the work while you live your actual life. That's real wealth, and that's worth far more than a fancy car or expensive house or whatever else society tells you that you're supposed to want. Build your systems, automate your wealth building, then just focus on living. Your future self will thank you for having the discipline to do this the right way, the rights.
script.analysis: Full 20467 canonical characters read. Anti-burnout wealth roundup: hook on obsessive grinding, rich-people myth, scarcity vs abundance mindset, goals, budgeting, automation thesis with a $75K worked example, emergency fund (Vanguard $2,000/21%), compounding $10K example, index vs active, dividends, real estate, diversification, high-interest debt and avalanche, tax-advantaged accounts, close. Verified/supported: Vanguard 21%, SPIVA direction, compounding examples reproduce, HSA triple advantage. Wrong or stale: one-year savings ($2,400 vs $10,400), leftover cash ($100-400 vs $1,400), IRA limit ($7,000 vs 2026 $7,500), card interest understated, 401(k) "tax-free". Generic advice, few sources named. Stored ending garbled.

claim_audit.claim: $75,000/year is about $2,300 every two weeks after tax; after automatic transfers of $400, $300 and $200 you are left with about $100 to $400.
claim_audit.stored_text_witness:
let's say you make $75,000 a year.

claim_audit.assessment: K02: 75,000/26 = $2,884.62 gross per paycheck; $2,300 implies ~20% withholding (plausible, not verified). 2,300 - 900 = $1,400 left, not "$100 to $400" (likely ASR garble of $1,400). UNVERIFIED_CREATOR_ASSERTION

claim_audit.assessment: K02: minimum = interest + 1% of balance -> $4,151 interest over 60 months with $2,736 still owed; a fixed 60-month payoff ($138.09/month) -> $3,286 interest. "$2,800" is understated under both conventions. 22% is consistent with G.19 rates.
